text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said on Wednesday that it saw opportunities in Lithuania as it caught up with its Baltic neighbours but saw the privatisation of state banks as uninteresting.
UBS on Tuesday became the Lithuanian government's adviser in the sell-off of Lithuanian Telecom shares on Tuesday.
"When you look at the two other Baltic states, you can see that there is plenty of upside," UBS representative Rafal Sosna told Reuters.
"They (Lithuania) have to sort of catch up a little bit with the pack. It's good news, it can only grow," he added.
But he was downbeat about the country's three state banks.
"(Lithuanian State) Commercial Bank, my understanding is basically it has a huge negative factor and nobody really wants to touch it," he said.
"The state Savings (Bank), I don't think that will be privatised," Sosna added. "The Agricultural Bank, it's also a big question mark. So I don't know how many banks are there for privatisation."

Lithuania chose to privatise its most troubled bank, Lithuanian State Commercial Bank, first, but the government failed to receive any replies by the first deadline, which was then extended to August 7.
The government had to inject 165 million litas worth of fresh share capital into State Commercial last year after it teetered on the brink of crisis.
Lithuanian Agricultural Bank is up second for privatisation, and officials have said the privatisation of Savings Bank would depend on the success of the first two sell-offs.
Although the state-owned banks do not look promising, UBS sees other areas of interest in Lithuania, Sosna said.
He said UBS had already been active with Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank in correspondent banking and was looking to get involved in other projects.
"We have have a couple of things in the pipeline here in Lithuania, but I have to keep that confidential," Sosna said.
